newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's BHP reports big slide in net profit.
newsitem.headline: Australia's BHP reports big slide in net profit.

text.p: Australia's largest listed company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), on Friday reported a steep dive in net annual profit in a result eroded by huge abnormal losses.

The steel, mining and petroleum group announced a 60.8 percent fall in earnings after abnormal items to just A$410 million (US$307 million) for the year ended May 31, after slicing over A$800 million from the book value of its global asset base.
BHP said the write-downs, including A$550 million at its North American copper assets and A$220 million in steel, blurred an otherwise improved result.
"Abnormal items have severely affected results that were otherwise an overall improvement on last year though not at the same level as achieved in 1995," the company said in its results statement.
Pre-abnormal profits rose A$93 million to A$1.39 billion, compared with analysts forecasts of between A$1.35 billion to A$1.4 billion.
Brokers said the market welcomed BHP's decision to write down the values of its assets.
"I think the market was relieved that they're wiping the slate clean," said BNP Equities head of equities John Bowie Wilson.
This was reflected in a 16 cent rise in the share price to A$19.22 in volatile morning trade.
"People are regarding it as responsible management," Bowie Wilson said. "Otherwise it's market neutral."
BHP said it was confident of an improved performance following the write-downs, which managing director John Prescott said would enable the group to better capitalise on its strengths.
Prescott said BHP was in a transition phase, and some of the assets written down might have no future with the group.
"We have sought to bring to account all the issues we have to deal with over the next two or three years that we think will affect our accounts," he said.
